subject: English Grammar
text: Fill in the blank: Fire and water ___ not agree.
explanation: Two distinct plural or incompatible subjects joined by 'and' require a plural verb ('do').

subject: English Grammar
text: Fill in the blank: Not only the teacher but also the students ___ present. (UP B.Ed 2024)
explanation: When correlative conjunctions like 'not only... but also' join subjects, the verb agrees with the closer subject ('the students', which is plural).

subject: English Grammar
text: Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error: 'If he will come (A) / I shall (B) / help him. (C) / No error (D)' (UP B.Ed 2021)
explanation: In conditional sentences, simple present ('If he comes') must be used in the conditional clause, not future tense.

subject: English Grammar
text: Identify the part that has an error: 'He is senior (A) / than me (B) / in service. (C) / No error (D)' (UP B.Ed 2022)
explanation: Latin adjectives like 'senior' are followed by the preposition 'to', not 'than'. Hence, 'than me' should be 'to me'.

subject: English Grammar
text: Identify the error: 'He has been (A) / playing football (B) / for morning. (C) / No error (D)' (UP B.Ed 2020)
explanation: 'Morning' is a point in time, which requires the preposition 'since' instead of 'for'.

subject: English Grammar
text: Find the error in the sentence: 'Unless you do not (A) / work hard, (B) / you cannot pass. (C) / No error (D)' (UP B.Ed 2019)
explanation: 'Unless' has a negative meaning itself. Using 'do not' creates a double negative. It should be: 'Unless you work hard'.

subject: English Grammar
text: Find the error: 'The scenery of (A) / Kashmir are (B) / very beautiful. (C) / No error (D)' (UP B.Ed 2018)
explanation: The noun 'scenery' is an uncountable singular noun, so the singular verb 'is' must be used instead of 'are'.

subject: English Grammar
text: Identify the error: 'None of the two (A) / candidates (B) / was selected. (C) / No error (D)'
explanation: When referring to exactly two options or people, 'neither' is used instead of 'none'. Hence, 'Neither of the two' is correct.

subject: English Grammar
text: Find the error: 'He walked (A) / ten miles (B) / by foot. (C) / No error (D)'
explanation: The correct prepositional phrase is 'on foot', not 'by foot'.

subject: English Grammar
text: Identify the error: 'Many a student (A) / have passed (B) / the exam. (C) / No error (D)'
explanation: The determiner 'Many a' must be followed by a singular verb. 'have passed' should be corrected to 'has passed'.

subject: English Grammar
text: Find the error: 'Although he worked hard, (A) / but (B) / he failed. (C) / No error (D)' (UP B.Ed 2023)
explanation: 'Although' is paired with 'yet' or a comma, not 'but'. We should remove 'but' or replace it with 'yet'.

subject: English Grammar
text: Find the error: 'Neither the teacher (A) / nor the students (B) / was present. (C) / No error (D)'
explanation: The verb should agree with the closest subject ('the students', which is plural). Therefore, 'was' should be replaced with 'were'.

subject: English Grammar
text: Find the error: 'I prefer (A) / coffee (B) / than tea. (C) / No error (D)' (UP B.Ed 2017)
explanation: The verb 'prefer' takes the preposition 'to' when making comparisons. It should be: 'to tea'.

subject: English Grammar
text: Identify the error: 'He has (A) / no other aim (B) / but to succeed. (C) / No error (D)'
explanation: The adjective 'other' is paired with the conjunction 'than', not 'but'. Thus, 'but to succeed' should be 'than to succeed'.

subject: English Grammar
text: Find the error: 'Each of these boys (A) / play (B) / games. (C) / No error (D)'
explanation: 'Each of' is grammatically singular and takes a singular verb. The verb 'play' should be corrected to 'plays'.

subject: English Grammar
text: Find the error: 'The cattle (A) / is grazing (B) / in the field. (C) / No error (D)' (UP B.Ed 2024)
explanation: 'Cattle' is a plural noun and takes a plural verb. Therefore, 'is grazing' should be corrected to 'are grazing'.

subject: English Grammar
text: Find the error: 'He is (A) / one of the best men (B) / that has ever lived. (C) / No error (D)'
explanation: The relative pronoun 'that' refers to the plural antecedent 'men', requiring a plural verb 'have ever lived' instead of 'has'.

subject: English Grammar
text: Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error: 'She has been (A) / working here (B) / since five years. (C) / No error (D)'
explanation: 'Five years' is a duration of time. Therefore, we should use the preposition 'for' instead of 'since'.

subject: English Grammar
text: What is the synonym of the word 'Abundant'? (UP B.Ed 2021)
explanation: 'Abundant' means existing or available in large quantities; 'plentiful' is its direct synonym.

subject: English Grammar
text: Find the antonym of the word 'Barren'. (UP B.Ed 2022)
explanation: 'Barren' means land that is too poor to produce vegetation; 'fertile' (productive) is its opposite.

subject: English Grammar
text: Choose the synonym of the word 'Diligent'. (UP B.Ed 2019)
explanation: 'Diligent' means showing care and conscientiousness in one's work; 'hardworking' is a direct synonym.

subject: English Grammar
text: What is the antonym of the word 'Rigid'? (UP B.Ed 2020)
explanation: 'Rigid' means stiff, unbending, or strict; 'flexible' is the antonym.

subject: English Grammar
text: Choose the synonym of the word 'Brief'. (UP B.Ed 2018)
explanation: 'Brief' means lasting for a short time or using few words; 'short' is its synonym.

subject: English Grammar
text: What is the antonym of the word 'Genuine'? (UP B.Ed 2023)
explanation: 'Genuine' means real, authentic, or honest; 'fake' or 'spurious' is the antonym.

subject: English Grammar
text: Choose the synonym of the word 'Candid'.
explanation: 'Candid' means truthful, straightforward, and frank.

subject: English Grammar
text: Find the antonym of the word 'Transient'.
explanation: 'Transient' means lasting only for a short time; 'permanent' is the antonym.

subject: English Grammar
text: What is the synonym of the word 'Adversity'? (UP B.Ed 2017)
explanation: 'Adversity' refers to a state of hardship or misfortune; 'misfortune' is a synonym.

subject: English Grammar
text: What is the antonym of the word 'Hostile'.
explanation: 'Hostile' means unfriendly or antagonistic; 'friendly' is the antonym.

subject: English Grammar
text: Choose the synonym of the word 'Vague'.
explanation: 'Vague' means thinking or communicating in an unfocused or unclear way; 'unclear' is its synonym.

subject: English Grammar
text: What is the antonym of the word 'Optimist'?
explanation: An 'optimist' looks at the bright side of things, while a 'pessimist' is someone who habitually expects the worst.

subject: English Grammar
text: Choose the synonym of the word 'Lethargic'.
explanation: 'Lethargic' means lacking energy; sluggish or apathetic.

subject: English Grammar
text: What is the antonym of the word 'Polite'? (UP B.Ed 2024)
explanation: 'Polite' means showing behavior that is respectful and considerate; 'rude' is its opposite.

subject: English Grammar
text: What does the idiom 'To bite the dust' mean? (UP B.Ed 2021)
explanation: The idiom 'To bite the dust' means to fall dead, fail, or be defeated in a competition or battle.

subject: English Grammar
text: What is the meaning of the idiom 'A blessing in disguise'? (UP B.Ed 2022)

options.A: A bad thing that turns out to be good

explanation: 'A blessing in disguise' is an apparent misfortune that eventually has good results.

subject: English Grammar
text: What is the meaning of the idiom 'To burn the candle at both ends'? (UP B.Ed 2019)

options.B: To work extremely hard or late

explanation: 'To burn the candle at both ends' means to exhaust oneself by working late and rising early.

subject: English Grammar
text: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom 'At the eleventh hour'. (UP B.Ed 2020)
explanation: 'At the eleventh hour' means at the last possible moment before it is too late.

subject: English Grammar
text: What does the idiom 'To break the ice' mean? (UP B.Ed 2018)

options.B: To start a conversation in an awkward situation

explanation: 'To break the ice' means to do or say something to relieve tension or start a conversation in a social setting.

subject: English Grammar
text: Choose the meaning of the idiom: 'Spill the beans'.
explanation: 'Spill the beans' means to disclose secret information, especially unintentionally or prematurely.
